column7: SMTPDelivery.newClient (setup-link email, run inside the admin's create-user request) and notifychan's EmailSink.newClient used go-mail's SMTPAuthAutoDiscover, which picks SCRAM whenever the relay lists it, with or without TLS; go-mail takes the PBKDF2 iteration count from the relay's server-first message and runs it with no bound, and an I/O timeout does not interrupt CPU work. A relay (or anyone on a tls=none path) announcing i=2147483647 therefore held the request for minutes of CPU. Mechanism selection moved to internal/smtpauth: SCRAM, PLAIN and LOGIN only over TLS (without TLS only CRAM-MD5 and NTLM, which never send the password and cost nothing to answer), and over TLS a SCRAM count above 1,000,000 is refused before any key derivation (TestSCRAMRefusesHugeIterationCountBeforeDeriving; placement of the count cannot evade it: TestScramIterationsReadsEveryCount). Red before the change (a relay announcing i=2147483647 over a connection without TLS: still deriving a key after 5 s), green after (under 100 ms, no AUTH SCRAM line sent). The upstream finding stays pinned at the library by TestGoMailFindingSCRAMIterationsUnbounded; the fuzz target FuzzSetupLinkHostileSMTPServer no longer exempts large counts. Not covered: a real TLS connection (the in-memory relay cannot speak TLS); SCRAM-*-PLUS is no longer offered (a custom smtp.Auth is not given the TLS state for channel binding).
